title: How Next.js Works
summary: File-based routes, server and client components, data fetching and route handlers.

steps.title: Routes are folders
body: **Next.js** is a framework on top of React. In its **App Router**, the folder structure under `app/` **is** the URL structure:
├── layout.tsx                 wraps every page (html, body, nav)
Each `page.tsx` has a **default export**: the component for that URL. Square brackets are **dynamic segments**, passed to the page as `params`:
export default async function Post({ params }: { params: Promise<{ slug: string }> }) {
Compare ASP.NET Core: this is attribute routing (`[Route("blog/{slug}")]`), except the route comes from the file's location.

steps.prompt: Match each file to the URL it serves.

steps.title: Server and client components
body: In the App Router, components are **Server Components** by default. They run on the server (at build time or per request), can be `async`, can read databases and secrets directly, and send only HTML to the browser. Zero JavaScript ships for them.
const res = await fetch("https://api.example.com/todos", { next: { revalidate: 60 } });
A component that needs **interactivity** (state, effects, event handlers, `localStorage`) starts with the directive `"use client"` and also runs in the browser:

The pattern: fetch on the server, pass data as props down to small client components for the interactive bits. Props crossing that boundary must be serializable (JSON-like: no functions, no class instances).

items: renders a static blog post from Markdown

steps.prompt: A Server Component passes `onSave={() => save()}` to a Client Component. What happens?
options: It fails: functions are not serializable across the server/client boundary
It works like any React prop
The function runs on the server when the button is clicked, automatically
Next.js converts it to a fetch call
steps.explain: Only serializable data crosses. (Next.js has **Server Actions**, functions marked `"use server"`, for calling the server from a form or button, but a plain function prop is not allowed.)

steps.prompt: Every page needs the same header, nav and footer. Where does that markup go in the App Router?
options: `app/layout.tsx`, which wraps every page below it via `children`
a `"use client"` component imported by each page
steps.explain: Layouts nest: `app/blog/layout.tsx` wraps only the blog pages, inside the root layout. They stay mounted while you navigate between their pages.

steps.title: Match a route
prompt: Write `matchRoute(pattern: string, path: string)` that works like Next.js segments. It returns the params object, or `null` when the path does not match.
- static segments must be equal: `"/about"` matches `"/about"` (`{}`)
- `[name]` matches one segment: `"/blog/[slug]"` with `"/blog/hello"` gives `{ slug: "hello" }`
- `[...name]` (only as the last segment) matches one or more segments as an array: `"/docs/[...path]"` with `"/docs/a/b"` gives `{ path: ["a", "b"] }`
- trailing slashes are ignored; segment counts must otherwise line up
starter: function matchRoute(pattern: string, path: string): Record<string, string | string[]> | null {
solution: function matchRoute(pattern: string, path: string): Record<string, string | string[]> | null {
template: Dojo.eq("catch-all needs one segment", null, matchRoute("/docs/[...path]", "/docs"));
hints: Split both on `/` and drop empty strings with `.filter(Boolean)`.
Walk the pattern segments; a catch-all takes `u.slice(i)` and returns immediately.
At the end, the two lengths must be equal.

steps.title: A route handler
prompt: Next.js `route.ts` files export functions named after HTTP methods. Write the logic of `GET /api/todos?done=true&q=tea` as a pure function:
`handleGetTodos(todos: Todo[], url: string)` returning `{ status: 200, body: Todo[] }`, filtered by the optional query parameters:
- `done=true` / `done=false` filters by done; any other value of `done` returns `{ status: 400, body: { error: "done must be true or false" } }`
- `q` keeps todos whose title contains it (case-insensitive)
starter: type Todo = { id: number; title: string; done: boolean };
function handleGetTodos(todos: Todo[], url: string): { status: number; body: unknown } {
solution: type Todo = { id: number; title: string; done: boolean };
function handleGetTodos(todos: Todo[], url: string): { status: number; body: unknown } {
return { status: 400, body: { error: "done must be true or false" } };
template: const dojoT = [{ id: 1, title: "Green tea", done: true }, { id: 2, title: "Cake", done: false }, { id: 3, title: "Iced TEA", done: false }];
Dojo.eq("no filters", { status: 200, body: dojoT }, handleGetTodos(dojoT, "/api/todos"));
Dojo.eq("bad done", { status: 400, body: { error: "done must be true or false" } }, handleGetTodos(dojoT, "/api/todos?done=yes"));
